question: Does the built-in browser refresh the tool list mid-session, without a page reload?
verdictScope: MEASURED at the BROWSER layer on the installed Chrome 152 against the remote origin: the tool surface goes 5 -> 6 on one un-reloaded document and the browser PUSHES WebMCP.toolsAdded naming probe_extra to an already-attached client 1 ms after the invoke was sent, unprompted and with no poll. The CLIENT layer is a separate reading and a weaker one: in the ChatGPT desktop built-in browser a human saw the sixth tool on the agent's NEXT TURN of the same conversation. Both point the same way and neither licenses the phrasing BW-33 bans. THE NARRATION CONSTRAINT IS UNCHANGED AND UNRELAXED: no document, storyboard, video cue or Devpost answer may claim the surface changes instantly; the honest phrasing stays "on its next turn".

observationPair.note: The accept's pair. Both observations are Runtime.evaluate readings of (await document.modelContext.getTools()).length under awaitPromise:true (IR-18 — the un-awaited form is recorded beside each and reads "undefined"), cross-checked against the surface enumerated from WebMCP.toolsAdded/toolsRemoved. The sixth tool was registered BETWEEN them by invoking probe_flip BY NAME over the CDP WebMCP domain (IR-17/19), never through Runtime.evaluate and never by document.modelContext.executeTool(name, args), which throws.
observationPair.gapNote: Wall clock between the two observations, end to end, including the completed probe_flip round trip. It is small because nothing in the path waits: the flip answered in 1 ms and the toolsAdded push arrived in 1 ms. An earlier run of this rig reported a 4048 ms gap; that number was an artifact of a defect in the rig's own push detector and is NOT reported here. See kb/pits/V2.md.

noReloadProof.note: Two independent witnesses that the pair was taken on ONE document instance. A reload would discard window.__v2_nonce and would emit a second Page.frameNavigated.

flip.note: probe_flip is code the system is supposed to RUN, so this records it running. A completed WebMCP.toolResponded with a MATCHING invocationId is the only field that discriminates a live surface from an empty launch (IR-17); the tool's own returned text is the page speaking.

content.text: probe_extra is now REGISTERED. List your tools again.

push.note: THE FINDING THAT SEPARATES THE TWO LAYERS. Chrome 152 does not make an attached client poll: it emits WebMCP.toolsAdded for probe_extra unprompted. So the next-turn behaviour seen in the ChatGPT built-in browser is a CLIENT POLICY, not a browser limitation — the same shape of finding as V6-consent-gate, and it closes nothing. A different client, or a future version, may behave differently. Also MEASURED here: toolsAdded fires ONE EVENT PER registerTool CALL (six events, one tool each), where H2's single-tool fixture could only show one event carrying a one-element array. Neither channel contradicts the other.

environment.originNote: THE REMOTE ORIGIN, DELIBERATELY. A green localhost run is not evidence in this project: V6-consent-gate is a finding that localhost hid entirely, and the prior V2 reading below was taken on http://localhost:8795.
environment.cdpDomainEnabledNote: RECORDED AND NEVER ASSERTED ON. WebMCP.enable returns OK with no flag, no tools and no page API at all (FACTS §1 IR-16(b), retracted claim). Nothing in this file branches on it.
environment.negativeControlNote: No no-flag arm is run here, because a no-flag launch has no page API and therefore cannot produce a pair at all. The control for THIS pair is internal and stronger: the same document, read twice, differed only across the flip. The flag-vs-no-flag control on Chrome 152 is already MEASURED in evidence/H2-reachability.json and evidence/V0.json.
environment.agentConnectedNote: No agent was connected to this browser. These are renderer-side readings only, and registerTool returns a Promise resolving to undefined in that condition.

reproduction.note: The rig is a THROWAWAY and is deliberately NOT in the repo: V2's only declared output is evidence/V2.json, and harness/** was out of scope for this dispatch. The CDP sequence is recorded here so the pair is auditable and re-runnable without it. The launch flags come from tools/chrome.mjs scenario `cdp` (H1), imported and not re-derived, so the run carries a label.
steps: subscribe to WebMCP.toolsAdded / toolsRemoved / Page.frameNavigated BEFORE navigating — toolsAdded fires at registration time
Page.navigate to the remote origin; await Page.loadEventFired
WebMCP.invokeTool {frameId, toolName:"probe_flip", input:{}} -> {invocationId}; await the MATCHING WebMCP.toolResponded
await the WebMCP.toolsAdded naming probe_extra (bounded; its absence would itself be the measurement)
OBSERVE after: same two reads, plus window.__v2_nonce and the navigation count

confirmingRerun.note: NOT the graded pair. An independent second run of the identical sequence, recorded because a single run of a rig that had already been wrong once is not worth much. It agrees exactly.

builtInBrowserReading.note: TRANSCRIBED from the previous evidence/V2.json, not re-run and not altered. It is the CLIENT layer reading and it is the one that answers the node title literally, since the ChatGPT built-in browser cannot be driven by CDP (HANDOVER §3 rule 8). graph.json R-43 already grades it: a manual reading, decisive enough to steer the design and NOT sufficient to close this node — it carries no before-count and no wall-clock gap, which is exactly what the pair above supplies. No document may cite it as a passed gate.
builtInBrowserReading.client: ChatGPT desktop built-in browser, model 5.6 Sol
builtInBrowserReading.method: probe_flip registered a sixth tool at runtime via registerTool with an AbortController signal; the agent was then asked to list tools again without reloading.
builtInBrowserReading.agentAnswer: Yes - probe_extra is now available. The page exposes six tools.

openItems: The CLIENT-layer reading has NOT been re-run on the remote origin. It was taken on http://localhost:8795 in Chromium 151, and V6-consent-gate is proof that this client's behaviour differs between localhost and a remote origin. The graded pair above is on the remote origin but is Chrome 152 with no agent attached, so it does not discharge this. Re-reading the tool list in the built-in browser on https://webmcp-probe.onrender.com after a probe_flip is a HUMAN action and would fold naturally into the next attended session; V2 is not listed in graph.json.human_gated, so no such session is currently scheduled. Recorded as open, not closed.
The built-in browser is Chromium 151 and the graded pair is Chrome 152. Two engines. The gap is recorded, not resolved — the same gap graph.json R-43 already records for the whole V lane.
